intro.t: The last word before four hundred years of silence.
b: A dispute-format book: God makes a charge, the people answer back, God responds. Half-hearted worship, broken marriages and withheld offerings. It ends looking forward to a messenger who will prepare the way — which is where Mark begins.

3.t: The forerunner who prepares the way — the verse Mark opens his Gospel by quoting.
The one place God invites his people to test him. Note the context: robbery, not investment.

4.t: The last words of the Old Testament look forward to a coming messenger, and four hundred years of silence follow.

1.t: Try offering it to your governor, God says. The animals were technically sacrifices and nobody was giving anything up.

2.t: In a passage about men discarding the wives of their youth. The context is faithlessness, and the language is strong.
